Itemize → the model (`qbo.map-invoice-lines`, agent mode, reads the invoice and bill only through tools) chooses an item or one of the bill's own accounts per line, nothing else; `docs.bill-lines` builds the lines in code with the invoice's descriptions, quantities, prices and amounts and refuses a missing, repeated or off-bill choice or an item line that isn't qty × price; then three actions, each `approval: required`, one after another: `qbo.bill.update_lines` (all lines replaced, total unchanged), `qbo.attachable.upload` (skipped when the document is the bill's own synced attachment), and, for a bill with no memo, `qbo.bill.update_memo` with "<vendor> invoice <number>, PO <po>" after reading the bill again for its new SyncToken. A notice ends it, citing the document, its reading and the transaction. // DECISION |
| Bill clerk: platform pieces | No migration. `matchBill`, `planBill` and `billLines` in packages/documents (`bill.ts`), as the read tools `docs.match_bill`, `docs.plan_bill`, `docs.bill_lines` and tool-mode skills of the same names (hyphenated); `DocumentsPort.matchBill`. The agent-mode skill `qbo.map-invoice-lines` ships with the connector (`qbo/skills.ts`) and apps/api registers it where qbo is registered. The notify step gains optional `sources` (templates resolving to ids or lists of ids), stored as the message's sources, so a notice can cite its records (invariant 10). The match reads the synced bills, not QuickBooks' query API: the vendor link and our transaction ids live there; a bill entered in QuickBooks reaches us within a minute (webhook) or 15 (CDC), so an invoice uploaded before that asks the client admin. // DECISION |
| Bill clerk: open | An invoice read twice while the first run still waits on approval asks for the same approvals twice (the second writes find the bill done and write nothing; a run after the first finished sees a done bill and proposes nothing); accounts beyond those on the bill need a chart-of-accounts read tool; learned item mappings per client (memory is off); installing the template on production by hand, where the seed never runs; the walk against the sandbox company. |

### 1.31 Decisions made while building M10 (Gmail, send only; 2026-11-05)

Built on `claude/m10-gmail-send`, with no migration: the connection's config and the vault hold
everything. Facts about Google we couldn't check, and the list to verify before a client connects,
are in `packages/connectors/src/gmail/NOTES.md`.

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Scopes | `gmail.send` and `openid email`, nothing else. `gmail.send` alone can't read which address signed in (the profile needs a read scope), and we need it to show the mailbox on Connections and to send From it; the ID token in Google's token answer carries it. `openid` and `email` are Google's basic sign-in scopes, not Gmail scopes. The privacy policy says so. The owner adds both to the consent screen beside `gmail.send`. // DECISION |
| Sign-in | Authorization code with `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent` (a refresh token on every consent, reconnects included) and `include_granted_scopes=false`. The callback refuses, storing nothing, a grant without `gmail.send` (Google's granular consent lets a person untick it), a grant with any other scope, an unverified address, and an ID token for another client id. The refusal is 422 `sign_in_refused` with plain words (`SignInRefusedError`, new in the connector framework). The ID token's signature isn't checked: it comes straight from Google's token endpoint over TLS. // DECISION |
| Redirect | Google's client registers `<origin>/api/connections/gmail/callback` per environment (owner, 2026-11-05), so Gmail returns to that API path, `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` when set, else built from `APP_ORIGIN`. `GET /api/connections/:connector/callback` only forwards the query to the portal's `/connections/:connector/callback` page (no store, no referrer), which posts it to the existing callback route in the person's session, as for Zoho and Podio. No `wrangler.jsonc` change: the default matches every registered URI. // DECISION |
| Who connects | The client admin, or the person whose mailbox it is: a client user may connect Gmail (only Gmail, `PERSONAL_CONNECTORS` in apps/api) when no one else's Gmail is connected, and disconnect it only if they connected it. The portal shows Connect and Disconnect to them accordingly (`personal` and `connectedByYou` on the portal's connection). The operator never connects. One Gmail connection per client (v1's rule), so a client connects one mailbox: an agent's own, a shared one or a person's. // DECISION |
| Tokens | In the vault (the client's key), with the address and the granted scopes; `connection.config` holds only `{address, scopes: ["gmail.send"]}`. Refresh before expiry and once after a 401; `invalid_grant` marks the connection as needing a person (the supervisor's `connection.needs_attention`). Disconnect revokes the refresh token at Google (the whole grant), then drops the credentials; an already revoked token is not an error. // DECISION |
| `gmail.send` | External, verb `create`, behind approval by default, with the same input as `email.send` (`to`, `subject`, `text`, `replyTag`), so reach out builds one input for either email connection. Its before state is the email as it would go: contact, to, from, reply-to, subject and text. The contact checks (a contact of this client, email consent, not opted out) run in code before and again at the send, through the same `EmailServices` as Resend. Output adds Gmail's `threadId`. // DECISION |
| Sent once | Gmail takes no idempotency key and `gmail.send` can't list sent mail. So the send is recorded as started (`raw_record` `EmailAttempt`, one per key) before Gmail is called; a re-run returns the recorded email, and a started send with no record is never sent again: the action fails as unconfirmed and the operator gets an item to check the mailbox. `EmailServices` gains optional `startAttempt`, `attemptFor` and `replyAddress`; `gmail.send` refuses to run without them. // DECISION |
| The message | Built in code (`gmail/mime.ts`): `From` the connected address, `To`, `Reply-To` the client's forwarding address with `+<reach-out id>` (none while the client has no forwarding address), the subject as RFC 2047 encoded words when it isn't plain ASCII (at most 75 characters each, never splitting a character), `Date`, our own `Message-ID`, `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` in base64 with CRLF line endings. Header values can't carry line breaks; addresses and the Message-ID are checked. `raw` is URL-safe base64 with padding. // DECISION |
| Replies | They come back to the client's forwarding address through the tagged Reply-To and are matched as for Resend (§1.25): the tag, the client's stored address and the contact's own address. The reply's own words are cut at the quoted history, now also at Gmail's line above the quote in the portal's six languages ("El … escribió:", "Le … a écrit :", "Em … escreveu:", "Il … ha scritto:", "Am … schrieb …:"). // DECISION |
| Reach out | `CHANNEL_TOOLS.gmail = {email: "gmail.send"}`: the operator binds an agent's email channel to the client's Gmail connection like Resend's; Gmail carries email only. Language, approval of the plan, one external action per attempt, grants and human release are reach out's, unchanged: an agent whose grant turns `create` off, or a connection with human release on and no live release, sends nothing (`not_allowed` with the reason). Test runs send nothing. // DECISION |
| Portal | The Connections card says "Send email from your Gmail. We can't read your mailbox." in the reader's language (six languages; the English is the manifest's description). |
| Test email | "Send a test email" on a connected Gmail (2026-11-05; for clients checking the connection, and for Google's demo video of `gmail.send`): `POST /api/connections/gmail/test-send` in the portal, for the client admin and the person who connected the mailbox (`mayManage`'s rule), and `POST /api/ops/clients/:id/connections/gmail/test-send` in the back office for the Sandbox client only (403 `not_sandbox` elsewhere). Both bodies are strictly empty: the email goes from the connection's stored address to that same address, never anywhere else, and is refused (409 `no_address`) without one or when the tokens' address differs. Plain text in the reader's language (core's `GMAIL_TEST_WORDS`; English in the back office). The person's own action, not an agent's: no run, no approval gate; the connector's `sendToSelf` (not a tool) reuses its MIME and send code with the vault's tokens and refresh. At most one a minute per connection, counted from `connection_change` (`kind: "gmail_test_email"`, with who, `by: client` or `operator`, and Gmail's message id), the connection row locked meanwhile. No migration. // DECISION |
| Sandbox disconnect | The operator disconnects what they connected in the Sandbox client (Gmail, QuickBooks, Zoho CRM, Podio, and no-sign-in tools) from the back office's Connections page, after a confirm step: `DELETE /api/ops/clients/:id/connections/:connectionId`, 403 `not_sandbox` in any other client. Same disconnect as the portal's (revoked at the provider, best effort; credentials and the vault's read model dropped; row, matrix, bindings and history kept), recorded `by: operator`. In a real client only the client disconnects. // DECISION |

Open after M10: everything under "To verify" in `gmail/NOTES.md`, against Google's docs and a test
mailbox; the owner's consent screen (add `openid` and `email`), the GitHub secrets wired into
`deploy.yml` (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`; owner's PR) and Google's verification (the
live site, the demo video, the scope's reason); replying inside a Gmail thread; Gmail's daily
sending limits; a fluent speaker's review of the new strings; a walk in Chromium.

### 1.32 Billing statements: Mezonas works out the bill, Stripe bills it (owner, 2026-11-05)

Owner, 2026-11-05: "switch to us and we can do all the different parts internally, not in stripe".
Each agent has its own monthly price, set in Mezonas. Stripe only holds customers and invoices. It
sends each invoice, takes payment and tells us the outcome. There are no Stripe products, prices,
subscriptions or meters. **This supersedes §1.24's subscription, quantity, meter, price-id and
webhook decisions.** Credits stay as §1.24 has them: one credit is one cent of our cost, from unit
costs over `usage_daily`, each day rounded up. Migration 0016 is in its own PR (#72). All amounts
are USD, `numeric(14,4)` with a currency, and decimal.js in code.

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Where prices live | `billing_template_price` holds a template's monthly price and included credits. It is global like `billing_unit_cost`: every session reads it and only operator sessions write it. It is edited on the template's Settings tab and listed on `/ops/billing`. `billing_agent_price` holds a client agent's override, per client with forced RLS. Each override has a required note and records who set it and when. It is edited on the client agent's Settings tab. Every change to either table is written to `agent_change`, the agent's audit log (with `tenant_id` null for a template). `billing_setting` gains `default_agent_price`, `credit_price` and `auto_send`. `allowance_credits_per_agent` becomes the default included credits, since it means the same thing. The Stripe price ids, meter name and price snapshots stay in the table, unused. // DECISION |
| Placeholders | Default agent price $250.0000 a month with 2,000 credits. An extra credit costs $0.0200. Auto-send is off. Invoices are due in 30 days. No template has a price until the operator sets one. |
| Which price | The override applies first. Then the template's price, then the platform rule, then the defaults. The platform rule: a client agent forked from the **supervisor** template (`slug = supervisor`, `tenant_id` null, `SUPERVISOR_SLUG`) costs $0 and includes 0 credits. The supervisor is how platform agents reach a client (§1.28), and it is identified by its template. A price the operator sets on the supervisor template overrides the rule. An agent with no template (blank or copied) uses the defaults. Only USD prices are saved. // DECISION |
| Agent days | On the hourly cron pass at the usage sweep's minute (:07 UTC), each client set up for billing gets one `billing_agent_day` row per active client agent for today (UTC). An active client agent is `kind = client`, not a test copy, `status = active` and `run_status = active`. Each row snapshots the agent's name (service name, else agent name), its price, its credits and where the price came from. The insert is `on conflict do nothing`, so the first price seen that day sticks. The rows are never updated or deleted. A day counts if the agent was active at any hourly pass. Paused and retired days are not billed. Activating, pausing and retiring no longer call Stripe. // DECISION |
| Building | Each :07 pass builds the statement for the month just ended for every billing client that doesn't have one yet. That is normally on the 1st, after the rollup. A pass that failed is caught up an hour later. Building is idempotent: one statement per client and month (unique key). A client set up after the month ended gets no statement for it. Usage counts from the day the client was set up (`setUpAt`), so work done before billing is not charged. With auto-send on, a new statement is sent right after it is built. With it off, the statement waits as a draft. // DECISION |
| Agent lines | There is one line per agent, described by its name from the last billed day. The amount is the sum of the agent's daily prices ÷ the days in the month, rounded half up to cents once per line. A price change mid-month therefore prorates each price by its own days, and an agent active for 10 of 30 days pays a third. A zero-price line shows as "Included". |
| Extra usage | One "Extra usage" line on every statement: max(0, credits used − pooled allowance) × the credit price, rounded half up to cents. The pooled allowance is the sum, over each agent's billed days, of its credits ÷ the days in the month, rounded half up to whole credits once. The credit price is the one in the settings when the statement is built, and the statement keeps it. // DECISION |
| Test runs | Usage by test copies is excluded: template test runs run as test copies, which are separate agents (§1.5, §1.16). A client agent's own test runs are rolled up into the same `usage_daily` rows as its live runs and can't be told apart, so they are still billed. Open for the owner (separating them needs a column on `usage_daily`). |
| Adjustments | The operator can add adjustments to a draft whose send hasn't started: a description of up to 200 characters and an amount in whole cents, positive or negative, never zero. Adjustments can also be removed then. The statement's total is recomputed each time. A database trigger enforces this: lines can't be inserted, changed or removed once Stripe has the invoice, except that each line's Stripe invoice item id is set once. A statement whose total is negative can't be sent (422). |
| Statuses | `draft` → `sent` → `paid` / `payment_failed` / `void`. A statement whose total is zero is `nothing_due` and never goes to Stripe. That covers a zero total at build time, and a draft adjusted to zero, which becomes `nothing_due` when it is sent. `void` and `nothing_due` are final, and nothing goes back to `draft` (trigger). The operator can void a draft only while its send hasn't started. Once Stripe has it, a void happens in Stripe and comes back through the webhook. // DECISION |
| Sending | There are four steps. Each stores Stripe's id as soon as it comes back, and each has the Idempotency-Key `mezonas:<statement id>:<step>[:<line id>]`. (1) `invoice`: create a draft invoice with the customer, `collection_method=send_invoice`, `days_until_due`, `auto_advance=false`, `pending_invoice_items_behavior=exclude`, the currency, a description and metadata `statement_id`, `tenant_id`. (2) `item:<line id>`: one invoice item per non-zero line (`invoice=<id>`, amount in cents, description, the month as its period). Zero lines stay on our statement only. (3) `finalize`: store the number, links and due date. (4) `send`: mark the statement `sent`. A failure stops the send, keeps the ids already stored and records `send_error`. Sending again resumes at the first step not done. With auto-send on, the hourly pass also resumes any draft whose send has started. In a request, the send runs in the request's transaction and Stripe's errors are recorded rather than thrown, so the stored ids commit. If the Worker dies mid-request, the retry replays the same answers through the idempotency keys. // DECISION |
| Set-up | Setting up creates the Stripe customer, with the key `mezonas-customer-<tenant>` and an optional billing email. Nothing else is set up ahead of time. `tenant.settings.billing` keeps the customer id. Its subscription fields stay in old rows but are no longer read or written, and `billing_usage_report` stays in the database unused. |
| Webhook | The route stays `POST /api/billing/stripe/webhook` with the same signature check. Each event is stored once in `billing_event`. Handled: `invoice.finalized` (number, links and due date), `invoice.paid` → `paid`, `invoice.payment_failed` → `payment_failed`, `invoice.voided` → `void`, `invoice.marked_uncollectible` → `payment_failed` (still owed, not collected). The client is found by its customer id, else by the invoice's `metadata.tenant_id`. The statement is found by invoice id, else by `metadata.statement_id`. An event older than the last one applied changes nothing, and a later failure never undoes `paid`. Every other event, the old subscription events included, is acknowledged and dropped. // DECISION |
| Back office | `/ops/billing` shows the settings form (credit price, default agent price and credits, auto-send, days until due, unit costs) and template prices. It also shows every client's month so far: an estimate from the days recorded so far and the credits so far, with our cost. Statements to review are listed with their lines. On a draft the operator can add or remove adjustments, send it or void it, and there is "Send all drafts". The client page's Billing section has set-up (customer and email), each agent's price and where it comes from, the month so far, and the statements with Stripe's links. Routes: `GET /api/ops/billing`, `PUT …/settings`, `GET/PUT …/agents/:id/price`, `GET …/clients/:id`, `POST …/clients/:id/setup`, `POST …/statements/:id/adjustments`, `DELETE …/statements/:id/adjustments/:lineId`, `POST …/statements/:id/send`, `POST …/statements/:id/void`, `POST …/statements/send-drafts`. All are operator-only, and the contract test covers the 403s. |
| Portal | `/billing`, for the client admin only, shows the month so far by service (price, days, amount, or "Included"), credits included and used, extra credits and their price, and past statements. Each statement has its lines and Stripe's hosted page ("View and pay" while sent) and PDF. Drafts are not shown, nor statements voided before they were sent. It never shows our cost, tokens or prompts. The field names avoid the forbidden list, and the contract test and the key walk check this. The strings are in the six portal languages (§1.18). |

Open after §1.32: everything marked UNCHECKED in `stripe/NOTES.md` (docs.stripe.com was not
reachable from the build environment); the owner's real prices, credits and credit price; whether a
client agent's own test runs are billed; a statement for a month a client was set up part-way
through charges only the days recorded after set-up; a walk in Chromium.

### 1.33 Run page polish (owner's Bill clerk test run, 2026-11-06)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Summaries with an empty slot | `renderSummary` (core) answers null when any reference in a skill's or tool's summary has no value (missing, null or blank), and callers say the step without that part: the executor writes "<label>: done", runAgent keeps its fallback, a tool call has no summary. A summary is never a sentence with a gap ("total unchanged at"). A test run's write had `{ wouldHaveDone, actionId, before }` as its output, which no write tool's summary can fill. // DECISION |
| Test-run timeline | A test run's write (an action, or a skill that proposed one) is `done` with `notWritten` from the agent port; the executor, in one place for every tool, writes "Would itemize the bill (test run, not written)" from the step's name (`TIMELINE_WORDS.wouldWrite`, in the six languages). `notWritten` is ignored in a live run. // DECISION |
| Test-run notices | A test run's notify step sends nothing: no thread message (it used to post an operator-only message on the run's thread in the client's data; nothing showed it, in the portal or the back office), no email. The rendered text stays on the step's input for the run log, its output is `{ sent: false }` and the timeline says "Would say what changed (test run, not sent)" (`wouldSend`). The notify port keeps its audience check as a second guard. // DECISION |
| Polling | `usePoll` skips a tick while a load is still in flight. A reload aborts the request before it, so a 2 s poll on top of answers that took longer cancelled every answer, and the run page kept saying "Running" after the run was done. The run's end is committed in `run:finish` before the usage rollup, which is its own durable step (`run:usage`). // DECISION |
| Test-run input | The Input (JSON) boxes start blank with a `{}` placeholder; blank means `{}`. A prefilled `{}` left an extra `}` after anything typed or pasted into it. The box is a plain textarea (no spelling, capitals or autocorrect), checked as you type; invalid JSON is said under it and the run can't start. |
| Activate and pause | The status chip shows the agent as activate, pause or retire answered it, at once, until the screen's own copy of the agent catches up. "Checking activation…" only shows for an agent that isn't active or retired. |
### 1.34 Ops MCP: the back office as a Claude connector (owner, 2026-11-06)

The owner connects Claude (claude.ai custom connector) to `https://staging.mezonas.com/mcp` and
`https://app.mezonas.com/mcp`: the same code, each environment with its own WorkOS environment and
data. Operators only; a client-facing MCP server comes later and reuses the plumbing (the protocol,
bearer verification, `scopeOf`/`inScope`/`invokeRoute`, the output fence) with its own tools and
the portal scope. Modelled on the owner's Plenary Labs ops connector (untrusted-data blocks, two-step
writes, every action audited); no code, key or resource shared with it. Setup: docs/operations.md,
"MCP server".

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Transport | MCP Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` on apps/api, stateless: one JSON-RPC message per POST, answered with `application/json` (no SSE stream, no `Mcp-Session-Id`, no batches); notifications and client responses get 202; GET and DELETE 405 (`Allow: POST`); an unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` header 400. Serves 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26 (initialize echoes a served version, else the latest). Spec site not reachable from the build session: versions checked against `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.2, the rest from memory (UNCHECKED). // DECISION |
| Not the official SDK | ~200 lines in `src/mcp/protocol.ts` instead of `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`: it brings express, ajv, cors and their kin; its web-standard transport would work, but tools, sessions and SSE are more than this needs. The one new dependency is `jose` (~37 KB in the bundle) for JWT and JWKS. // DECISION |
| Authorization server | WorkOS AuthKit, per environment, is the OAuth 2.1 authorization server: MCP clients register with it (Dynamic Client Registration, switched on in WorkOS), use PKCE and its hosted sign-in, and get its access tokens. The Worker is only a resource server, so no OAuth server, refresh-token table, migration or new secret of ours; revocation is WorkOS's (end the session there) and membership is read on every call, so removing an operator takes effect at once. The fallback, a small authorization server in the Worker, is not built. AuthKit's MCP support was not reachable to check (UNCHECKED). // DECISION |
| Finding AuthKit | `WORKOS_AUTHKIT_DOMAIN` (a var in `wrangler.jsonc`, per environment; empty: `/mcp` and its metadata answer 404). The Worker reads `<domain>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414), requires its `issuer` to be the domain and takes `jwks_uri` from it; cached an hour per isolate, failures not cached. Needs WorkOS sign-in fully on in the same environment (else 503). // DECISION |
| Metadata | `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `…/mcp` (RFC 9728): `resource` `<APP_ORIGIN>/mcp`, `authorization_servers` [AuthKit], public with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` serves AuthKit's metadata again for 2025-03-26 clients. All three, and `/mcp`, are in `run_worker_first`. |
| Tokens | A 401 carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` (plus `error="invalid_token"` and a fixed description for a token that fails). A token must be a JWT signed RS256 or ES256 by AuthKit's JWKS, `iss` exactly AuthKit's issuer, `aud` containing `<APP_ORIGIN>/mcp` (RFC 8707; `MCP_AUDIENCE` overrides it if AuthKit names the resource differently, never turns the check off), unexpired, with a subject (60 s skew). packages/auth `bearer.ts`. A request without a token gets its 401 without waiting on AuthKit. // DECISION |
| Who | The token's `sub` is a WorkOS user id; it must already be an `app_user.workos_user_id` (someone who has signed in to that environment's back office once; MCP sign-in never provisions or claims an invitation), with an operator membership: 403 otherwise. The session is built as for `/api/ops` (`buildSession`, all served clients), and every tool runs in `withOperator` on those clients. // DECISION |
| Same code as the back office | Reads go through the back office's own handlers: `mount` now registers each handler, and `invokeRoute` runs one for a session without HTTP (`scopeOf` role and client scope, the route's Zod input schemas, `inScope` transaction, the response contract). Where no route answers (a feedback item with its screenshot, connections across clients) the tool queries inside the same operator scope and filters by `tenant_id`. `/api/ops/runs` gained `since`. Feedback resolve is one function (`resolveFeedback`) for both; its update now only changes a row still open. |
| Tools | Read: `whoami` (user, environment, served clients), `clients_list` (agents, open inbox, connections by status, latest health), `client_get` (details, agents, connections, members, health and open findings), `feedback_list` (open/resolved/all, client or back office), `feedback_get` (comment, page, pin, client, who, when, and the screenshot as an MCP `image` block from R2), `runs_list` (client, status, agent, mode, since), `run_get` (steps with summaries and output, tool calls, actions with before and result, inbox items, cost), `inbox_list`, `connections_list` (status, last sync, last change), `records_search` (the Records page's search), `marketing_report` (a client's Marketing report with its query; M44, §1.74). Write: `feedback_resolve` only. Large free-form JSON is clipped with a preview. |
| Untrusted data | All database text goes in one `<untrusted-data source="mezonas:<tool>">` block per result, as JSON with `<` and `>` escaped, so it can't close the block; only our own sentences, counts and the confirm token are outside it. The server instructions say what the blocks are and not to follow anything in them (invariant 9). Any field named like a secret (core's `FORBIDDEN_SECRET_FIELD`) is replaced as a second guard (invariant 13); the routes already leave secrets out. No `structuredContent`, so nothing bypasses the fence. // DECISION |
| Two-step writes | First call (no `confirm_token`): nothing changes; it previews and returns a token sealed with packages/auth's `seal` under its own purpose `mcp-confirm` (key from the environment's `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD`, so it can't be read, forged or used in another environment), bound to the user, tool and a hash of the canonical arguments, valid 5 minutes. Second call with the same arguments and the token: checked, its nonce claimed once in R2 (`operator/mcp/confirm/<nonce>`, no table), then the write. Replays, other arguments, other users and expired tokens are tool errors (`confirm_used`, `confirm_mismatch`, `confirm_expired`, `confirm_invalid`). // DECISION |
| Audit | One JSON log line per tool call (`event: "mcp.tool_call"`, `via: "mcp"`, environment, user id and email, tool, arguments with the token as `[token]`, outcome `ok`/`error`/`preview`/`done`, error code, target, duration), kept by Workers Logs. A resolve also sets `resolved_by` as the back office does. Not `agent_change`/`tenant_change`: most calls span clients and change nothing. HOOK: `AppDeps.mcp.audit` takes a sink that writes `audit_event` once #82 lands. // DECISION |
| Rate limit | 120 calls a minute per operator: Cloudflare's Rate Limiting binding `MCP_RATE_LIMIT` (namespaces 1100 local, 1101 staging, 1102 production); a per-isolate window where it is not bound or fails. 429 with `Retry-After: 60`. // DECISION |
| Config | Vars only (`WORKOS_AUTHKIT_DOMAIN`, optional `MCP_AUDIENCE`, in `wrangler.jsonc` and `.env.example`); no new secret, so `deploy.yml` is unchanged. |
| Later writes (not built) | Candidates, each two-step: reopen feedback; resolve an operator inbox item (approve/reject); retry a failed run; pause or activate a client agent; sync a connection now; resolve a request. A client-facing MCP server (portal scope, its own tools, no cost or bundles) after that. |

### 1.35 Built for HIPAA, SOC 2 and PCI DSS (owner, 2026-11-05)

Owner, 2026-11-05: "lets just make sure the tool is built for HIPAA compliance and PCI and SOC2, we
can work on the certification steps later". This section covers the technical controls only. The
BAAs, policies, risk assessment, training and audits come later and are not code. Four PRs, in this
order: CI, the migration (0017), sign-in, then the controls. HIPAA mode is per client. Every other
control applies to every client.

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| CI data | CI never connects to Neon, so client data never reaches a GitHub runner. It applies every migration to its own Postgres. (A schema-only Neon branch was the first plan; Neon refuses them on this project, since our SQL-made `cs_runtime` counts as a "legacy web access role".) A migration that only fails on real rows fails on staging first: `deploy.yml` migrates staging in a transaction before its Worker deploys. CodeQL (`security-extended`) runs on ready PRs, `main` and weekly. Dependabot opens monthly grouped updates for npm and Actions, majors included (owner, 2026-11-06: less noise); security updates come as GitHub learns of them. // DECISION |
| Audit log | `audit_event` (migration 0017) is append-only. It has a SELECT and INSERT grant only, plus a trigger that refuses UPDATE and DELETE for everyone. `mount` writes one row per request to every session route, reads included. Each row holds the actor (user id, email, role), the action (`GET /api/runs/:id`), the outcome and HTTP status, the target (route params and `?client=`, never bodies), the IP (`cf-connecting-ip`) and the user agent (first 256 characters). A successful request writes its row in the handler's own transaction, so a write and its audit row commit together. A refused or failed request writes its row in a short transaction of its own. Sign-in, sign-out and refused sign-ins are written by the session routes (`session.sign_in`, …). The row carries WorkOS's `authentication_method` and no client. `tenant_id` is the client acted in, or null for cross-client back-office lists and sign-ins. Rows with no client are read only in operator sessions. There are no foreign keys, so the log outlives a purged client. It holds ids, never content. Retention is 6 years (HIPAA §164.316(b)(2)). The operator reads the log at `GET /api/ops/audit` and on the back office's Audit log page. Clients don't see it in v1. Agents' own work is already audited by `run`, `step_run`, `tool_call` and `external_action`. Back-office reads and writes made through the Ops MCP server (§1.34, `invokeRoute`) write the same row, with the action `mcp GET /api/ops/…`, beside §1.34's log line. // DECISION |
| Access review | `GET /api/ops/access-review` (SOC 2 CC6.2, CC6.3) lists every user with their role in each client and their last sign-in, taken from the audit log. It is on the Audit log page. A review is done by reading it and removing what should go. // DECISION |
| Sessions | The idle limit is 30 minutes and the absolute limit 12 hours (was 30 days). These apply to everyone (HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iii), PCI DSS 8.2.8 at 15 minutes for card-data systems, which we aren't). The cookie gains `lat`, the last activity. A request moves it only when the app marks it as the person's own (`x-countersign-activity: 1`, sent when there was a key press, click or touch in the last minute), so background polling never keeps a session alive. The app also signs out by itself after 30 minutes without input. Older cookies, which have no `lat`, count their last refresh as activity. The Ops MCP server (§1.34) has no cookie: its WorkOS access tokens last 5 minutes and the AuthKit session behind them follows WorkOS's own limits (12 hours, 30 minutes idle). MFA is required in WorkOS (AuthKit → Authentication → Multi-factor, set to required; `docs/operations.md`). The app can't see whether a factor was used, so the sign-in audit row records the method. // DECISION |
| Sign-in callback | (2026-11-06, after the owner landed on "Sign-in did not finish" between sign-ins.) A refused `GET /api/auth/callback` says why in the audit row's `target.reason`: `callback_incomplete` (no `code` or `state` on the URL, e.g. WorkOS sent an error), `state_missing` (no state cookie, or one that doesn't open), `state_expired`, `state_mismatch` (another tab started a sign-in since), `code_rejected` (a used or expired code: Back, reload, a restored tab) or `workos_unavailable`; `target.next` says what followed. If the request already carries a valid session (the adapter's `identify`, rotated cookies kept), it goes to the app (the state's `return_to`, else `/`): a refused callback never makes a session, it only recognises one. Otherwise any of those but `callback_incomplete` starts sign-in again once: a redirect to `/api/auth/sign-in?return_to=…&retry=1`, which puts `2.` before the new nonce. The callback reads that mark from the `state` WorkOS echoes, not from a cookie, so a browser that drops cookies can't loop; a failure of a restarted sign-in, or a callback with no `state`, shows the sign-in page's error (`?error=unauthenticated`, as before). The mark is part of the nonce in the state cookie, so the CSRF check is unchanged: a sign-in finishes only with a matching, unexpired state. The state now lasts 30 minutes (was 10), for slow emailed-code steps. // DECISION |
| Sign-in page | (2026-11-10, the owner: "it does not make sense to have the account go in here".) With WorkOS, `/sign-in` goes straight on to `GET /api/auth/sign-in` (carrying `next` as `return_to`, replacing the history entry), so the first page a person sees is WorkOS's. The card shows only when a sign-in came back with `?error=`: the reason and the button to start again, so a refusal never loops. No "Create account" button of ours: sign-in admits invited addresses only, and an invited person makes their account from the invitation email; whether WorkOS's page offers sign-up is its dashboard setting. The dev sign-in is unchanged. // DECISION |
| Security headers | Every `/api` response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, HSTS (2 years, subdomains) and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. The app's static assets get the same, with a CSP that allows only the app's own origin, plus Sentry's ingest for errors (`apps/web/public/_headers`). The MCP endpoint and its `.well-known` metadata get the API's headers. // DECISION |
| HIPAA mode | `tenant.settings.compliance.hipaa`. Only the operator can turn it on or off, with a reason, logged in `tenant_change`. While it is on, the client's data may go only to the vendors ("processors") named in `BAA_PROCESSORS`. That is a Worker variable listing the vendors we have a signed BAA with, set by the owner when one is signed. The infrastructure vendors (Cloudflare, Neon, WorkOS) must be listed before any client can be put in HIPAA mode. Processors, in `packages/core/src/compliance.ts`: models go to `anthropic`, or to `openai` for `openai:` ids. The `twilio` connector goes to `twilio`, plus `meta_whatsapp` for `whatsapp.*` and `elevenlabs` for `call.*`. `resend` goes to `resend`. The client's own tools (QuickBooks, Gmail, Zoho, Podio, the client's webhook endpoints, browser sites) are the client's vendors, not ours, and need no listing. Sentry gets no client data by design (scrubbing, below), so it isn't a processor. Enforcement happens at four points. Turning HIPAA on is refused while a connector it doesn't cover is offered. Offering such a connector is refused. A run's model calls are refused when the provider isn't covered, and so is background document reading. A tool call is refused, through the runtime's generic `policy` hook, when its processors aren't covered. // DECISION |
| Card numbers (PCI DSS 3.3, 3.4) | Mezonas never takes card data. Billing uses Stripe-hosted invoices, and payment sites are blocked-tier for browser logins. Card numbers can still arrive in documents, texts and emails, so `redactCardNumbers` (core) replaces any 13–19 digit run that passes the Luhn check with `[card ending 1234]`. It runs in the Sentry scrubbers (API and app), on a document's extracted text and fields before they are stored, and on inbound texts before they are stored. The model may still read the number in the document; nothing of ours keeps it. // DECISION |
| Offboarding | `POST /api/ops/clients/:id/retire` takes a reason. It sets `tenant.retired_at`, logs a `tenant_change` and an audit row, retires every client agent and disconnects every connection (grants revoked at the provider, credentials removed). The Sandbox client can't be retired. Its operators still see it. From then on nobody signs in to the client, no run starts and inbound hooks for it are dropped. Thirty days later the hourly cron deletes the client's stored files (`tenants/<id>/` in R2). The owner then runs `pnpm --filter @countersign/db run db:purge-client -- <client id>` as `cs_owner`. It refuses to run before the 30 days have passed or before the files are gone. It deletes every row of the client in every table with a `tenant_id` except `audit_event`, in foreign-key order, disabling the history triggers for that one transaction. Tables that point at each other (an agent and its live version) have their nullable links cleared first. It then deletes the `tenant` row, and the client's users who belong to no other client, and records `client.purge` in the audit log. Data at other vendors (Twilio subaccount, ElevenLabs transcripts, Resend domain) is closed by hand from a checklist (`docs/operations.md`). Neon's point-in-time history expires on its own schedule. // DECISION |
| Exports | Three exports (terms §12: an export on request within 30 days after the service ends). **Client data export** (operator): `POST /api/ops/clients/:id/exports` starts `ExportWorkflow` (binding `EXPORT_WORKFLOW`), `GET` lists them, each ready one with a 5-minute link. The job reads each table a page at a time inside `withTenant(client)`, one durable step per page (and per batch of documents), and the last step streams a stored (uncompressed) ZIP of known size into R2 at `tenants/<id>/exports/<export id>/`. No table: the export's status is `export.json` beside it, and its start is in `tenant_change` and the audit log, its end in the audit log. It holds every record table as CSV (`apps/api/src/exports/tables.ts`, columns listed one by one: services, connections without credentials or settings, vendors, transactions and lines, documents, document readings, items read from documents, synced records, organizations, contacts and the change logs, live runs, the steps the client's timeline shows, external actions with before, change and result, inbox items and approvals that aren't the operator's, client and contact messages, knowledge versions), the original documents and a README. Never in it: credentials, the client's key, grants, release codes; agent bundles, skills, step inputs and outputs, tool calls and memory (Mezonas' work, and where instructions and prompts live; bundles stay out by default, owner, 2026-11-06); cost and tokens; test runs, operator items and notes, events, billing, feedback. JSON cells drop every forbidden field. A retired client can be exported until its files are deleted, and the hourly sweep waits while an export is being built (for up to a day). The ZIP is deleted with the client's files. **Accountant export** (`GET /api/exports/accountant?from=&to=`, client admin; the back office's `/api/ops/clients/:id/exports/accountant`): the period's external actions with system, tool, amount and currency where the change states one, who signed and when, run and agent version, before, change and result, and the documents they name by file name; a ZIP with the documents and runs, or `format=csv`. **Audit export** (`GET /api/exports/audit`, client admin): the client's own `audit_event` rows, never rows without a client. Periods are whole days in the client's timezone, at most a year; the accountant ZIP holds at most 100 MB of documents and 20,000 changes, the audit CSV 100,000 rows. Every export writes an audit row naming what it covered. No screens yet (the owner is redesigning the UI). // DECISION |
| Encryption | Connection secrets stay encrypted under each client's key (§1.26). Records and files rely on Neon's and R2's encryption at rest (AES-256) and on TLS in transit. Application-level encryption of records was considered and not done in this pass: neither HIPAA, SOC 2 nor PCI requires it once card numbers aren't stored. // DECISION |
| Notifications | Email and text notifications to people never carry record content: the count and a link to the inbox only. Today notices are thread messages and release codes carry only the code. This is a rule for when notification emails are built. // DECISION |

Not code, for the owner: BAAs (then `BAA_PROCESSORS`), MFA required in WorkOS, Cloudflare WAF rate
limiting on `/api/*`, GitHub's secret scanning with push protection and branch protection on `main`,
a tested restore from Neon's point-in-time history, and the policies and audits themselves.

### Run controls (W1-E)

Built from ARCHITECTURE v0.12 §10.10 and §14 and plan §1.40 (design branch). What the build decided
where those leave it open:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Files | `packages/core/src/api/runs-filter.ts` (RunFilter, its query parameters, how a run started), `run-controls.ts` (route specs, short ids, error keys, the carry rule, CSV fields); `packages/workflows/src/executor.ts` (resume, reuse, `errorKey`, `resumePoint`); `packages/agents/src/log/model-calls.ts` and `carried-actions.ts`, `runtime/carry.ts`; `apps/api/src/routes/run-controls.ts` (routes and RunFilter's SQL). Shared files touched in `// v0.12 W1-E` blocks: `routes.ts`, `app.ts`, `index.ts`, `call-tool.ts` (one call after the before state), `runs/ports.ts` (`retryOf`), `run-agent.ts` (the model-call loop), `contract.ts` (forbidden portal fields). |
| RunFilter keys | One key per §1.40 field, lists comma-separated (`statuses=failed,waiting`); the old names (`client`, `agent`, `status`; the portal's `service`) still work. `signedBy`, `changedConnector` and `errorKey` take one value; `attemptsOver` and `costOver` mean "more than". The portal refuses (400) `clients`, `templates`, `versions`, `mode`, `costOver`, `errorKey`, `groupBy`: it has one client, sees live runs only, and shows neither versions, cost nor error keys. // DECISION |
| How it started | From `run.trigger`: `schedule`; `event` (except the event types below); `webhook` (`webhook.received`), `message` (`inbound.message`, `thread.message_posted`, `account.request_passed`, and `/commands`), `handoff` (`run.succeeded`); `manual` when the operator started it, `person` when a client person did (`trigger.client`, or `trigger.startedBy.role` a client role). An ask's run matches none. // DECISION |
| Text | `text` matches a short id (`R-1a2b3c` or the six hex), the workflow slug, the agent's or service's name, or the error's words. |
| Attempts | The run and the runs it retried, back to the first (a recursive count over `retry_of`). A run is retried once (409 `already_retried` names the retry); a failed retry is retried in its turn, so the chain is a line. // DECISION |
| Resume | `resume_from` is the top-level step holding the failed node (`resumePoint`). The retry's load step reads the run retried's rows of the top-level steps before it; `succeeded` rows are copied as succeeded and `skipped` rows stay skipped (a write a person turned down is not reported as done), each with summary "reused from R-xxxxxx". A step before it with no row runs again. A failure before any step (no node) retries from the start. // DECISION |
| Carried approvals | A retry's write step looks at the actions the same node proposed in the run retried and the runs before it (keys `<run>:<node>:<n>`), after the gate (matrix, grant, the go-live stage through W1-A's `effectiveMode`, release) and the before state, by the hash of the input. `done`: never redone, its result returned. `approved`, `executing` or `failed` with an approval under 72 hours: reopened (`failed` → `approved`) and executed under its original key, its release checked for the retry's run. A failure whose write may have happened (`unconfirmed`) is never carried. A write the system approved (no signer) is carried only while the gate would still run it without asking, so a tightened matrix, or an agent moved back to trial or signoff, asks again; a person's signature stands while the gate allows the write. The carried action keeps its run; the retry's tool call links it, with `{approvedVia: 'retry_of', retryOf}` as its logged output. The step's idempotency index still advances, so a Workflow retry of the step finds its later writes by key. // DECISION |
| Cancel | Refused (409 `writing`) while an action of the run is `executing`; else `instance.terminate()` (an instance that ended or never started is fine), then in the request's transaction: the run `cancelled` (`error: {code: 'run_cancelled', by}`), open step runs `cancelled`, open items `expired`, proposed actions `rejected` with `{code: 'run_cancelled'}`. Approved actions not yet executing stay approved; the terminated run never claims them. A queued run cancelled before its instance starts ends at its load step without running. // DECISION |
| Replay | A test run of the same agent, version, workflow and payload in the run's own client, `trigger.replayOf` = the run. Any run can be replayed. |
| Error keys | `runErrorKey`: the failed action's tool id, else the step kind (`skill`, `person`, …) of the innermost step that failed, never a loop or fork around it, else `run` before any step; the code from the error's words (`refused`, `escalated`, `timeout`, `unauthorized` for 401 and expired sign-ins, `rate_limited`, …, an error class's name, else `failed`). Grouping: `coalesce(error->>'key', error->>'code', 'unknown')`, up to 100 groups, most frequent first, with client names and agent ids. // DECISION |
| CSV | `GET /api/ops/runs.csv` takes the list's filter, not its page size: up to 5,000 runs, newest first. Columns per §1.40, the id as the short id; written and served with the exports stream's `csvFile` and the exports stream's `mountFile` (core's `ExportFile`). // DECISION |
| Model calls | After each model call in `run-agent.ts`'s agent-mode loop, the runtime calls the `modelCalls` port with the request, the answer, usage and timing. The writer (`dbModelCalls`, in `src/log` with the other log writers) inserts the row in the client's transaction, then stores the body at `tenants/<id>/model-calls/<id>.json`: card numbers redacted (`redactCardNumbersDeep`), a document's inline base64 bytes left out with their size (the document is already stored). Cost is rounded up to 4 places. A body that fails to store is logged and the row stays. `packages/llm`'s `onCall` gains a second argument, `{request, response}`. // DECISION |
| Model calls beyond the loop (follow-up) | One helper (`recordModelCall`, `packages/agents/src/runtime/model-call.ts`) turns the model client's `onCall` into a row through the same port, used by the agent loop, a reach-out's message (`composeReachMessage`, on the reach-out's step with the agent version) and a document read in a step (`docs.extract`: the tool invocation's `recordModelCall`, wired by the gate like `recordUsage`). A call without a run step (a reach-out recorded with no step run) records nothing. Background reading (`extractInBackground`) keeps no row: `model_call.run_id` and `step_run_id` are NOT NULL with foreign keys and a background read has neither; its tokens and cost stay on `doc_extraction` and `usage_platform_daily` (§1.43). // DECISION |
| Saved views | `ops_runs` only; the filters are a RunFilter (400 otherwise); names unique per user (409 `name_taken`). Every route filters by `user_id` = the session user, since RLS only checks that the session is an operator's. |
| UI | Minimal, on existing classes: the run page shows the short id, Retry from the failed step, Cancel run, Replay as a test run, and the model calls table; the runs list gains "Failures by error", whose key filters the list. |
