**Skill model (2026-11-11): Reshape data** (owner's design; ARCHITECTURE §10.14 "Reshape data";
branch `skills/reshape`; no migration). One built-in deterministic skill, `data.reshape` ("Reshape
data"): any input in, an output whose fields the step defines, each a mapping (a copied input
field, a literal, or a typed expression). It never writes and calls no model when it runs. Core
`processes` (`process/reshape.ts`, `process/reshape-propose.ts`): `ReshapeMapping`, `ReshapeExpr`,
`evaluateReshape`, `reshapeOutputSchema`, `reshapeExprSchema`, `reshapeProblems`,
`schemaFitProblems`, `sampleFromSchema`, `reshapeContext`, `proposeReshape`, `wireToReshape`; core
`units` (`convertUnits`, `unitOf`). agents: the skill and its pure handler (`tools/reshape.ts`), the
runtime's Reshape branch, the Builder AI's suggestion (`builder/reshape.ts`). apps/api:
`POST /api/ops/agents/:id/reshape/propose` and `/reshape/sample` (`routes/ops-reshape.ts`). Web: the
inspector's mapping table (`reshape-step.tsx`), the offers (`reshape.ts`). Built-ins: 128.
- // DECISION: the expression set is the rule rows' calculations (copy, literal, today, days
  between, sum, difference, percent change, a bucket, here with its buckets inline since the step
  has no parameters) plus `formatDate` (iso, mdy, dmy, long), `formatNumber` (places, text or a
  number), `formatMoney` (a decimal string at 2 places by default, or an amount with a currency),
  `join`, `split`, `pick` (by index or where a field equals a value, then a field), `pluck`,
  `mapList` (a list of records field by field; `{item: …}` reads the item) and `convertUnit`. Data
  only, parsed by Zod; nothing executes text. The sums go through the rule rows' own evaluator
  (`evaluateSkillCompute`), so decimals, amounts in one currency and dates behave the same way.
- // DECISION: the mapping is the step's `reshape` field (`SkillStep.reshape`: output fields in
  order, each with its JSON Schema, `required` (absent: required) and `from`); the step's `input`
  brings in the sources under keys taken from the steps' names (`readDocument:
  "{{steps.read.output}}"`), and expressions read `input.<key>…`. Only a `data.reshape` step may
  carry one, and one must (`reshape_mapping`).
- // DECISION: the step's output is the mapping's fields (`stepOutputSchema`), so later steps type
  by it; the skill's own schemas are open. The validator types each field against what the input
  brings in (a field read that isn't there, a value that doesn't fit, a required field unmapped)
  and against the next step on its path when that step reads the Reshape step's output (a field it
  reads that the mapping doesn't give, a type it doesn't take, a required input left out). Every
  problem is an error with code `reshape_mapping` on the Reshape step, field `reshape.<name>`, so a
  version move of the step before or a change to the next step's input flags it by field.
- // DECISION: an empty value (missing or null) leaves an optional field out (an invoice with no
  due date makes a bill with none); a required one fails the step naming the field, unless its type
  allows null. Any field the mapping can't fill fails the step: never a partial output.
- // DECISION: a JS number read as money goes through its shortest decimal text, never its binary
  value; money text such as "$1,250.00" or "(12.50)" is read; rounding is half up (core's Decimal).
  An amount never changes currency in `formatMoney`.
- // DECISION: core gains a small unit table (`packages/core/src/units.ts`: length, mass, volume,
  counts, board feet; exact factors) for `convertUnit`. Materials keeps its own invoice-unit table:
  what a box or a pail holds is the vendor's, not a fixed conversion.
- // DECISION: the runtime runs the mapping through the skill's pure handler (`data.reshape`,
  `sideEffect: none`, `pure`), so the call is logged like any tool call and may run on the test
  bench; the executor hands the mapping to the agent port (`SkillStepRequest.reshape`), which
  passes it to `runAgent`. Today is the run clock's date in UTC, as for rule rows. The handler is
  not offered as a read step (`stepTools` leaves it out).
- // DECISION: the deterministic proposal maps by name first: exact, any case or spelling
  (`vendor.name` reads as `vendorName`), then a short synonym list for the fields our actions and
  skills name; a type must fit, or convert plainly (a number into money text or number text, text
  read as a number, a list of text joined, a list of records mapped field by field). A type alone
  never maps a field. The nearest step wins a tie. "Propose an updated mapping" keeps every field
  whose mapping still type-checks (`kept`) and proposes the rest.
- // DECISION: the Builder AI is asked once per proposal, for top-level fields still unmapped
  (a mapped list's leftover item fields are the operator's), on the Builder's model and path, in the
  route's request (never in a client's run). Its answer takes each expression as any JSON; each is
  parsed with `ReshapeExpr`, typed against the step's sources and fitted to its field, and dropped
  with a reason when it fails (shown to the operator). The call's cost is returned to the builder,
  not charged to the client. The hand-written replay is in `fixtures/llm`.
- // DECISION: samples come from the client agent's latest test or live run that stored a
  succeeded output for a step the Reshape input reads (its step rows, in the client's scope); a
  step that run didn't reach, and a template, are sampled from the schemas (`sampleFromSchema`).
- // DECISION (web): a Reshape step placed from the palette asks the server for its mapping once
  (by name, then the Builder AI); the offers ("Add a Reshape step before this" on a step whose own
  input errors say earlier steps can't fill it; "Add a Reshape step" after a skill whose output
  fills at least two of a write's fields, one required, by the proposal, where it doesn't fit
  whole) place it pre-filled with core's deterministic proposal and wire the next step, and the
  operator asks the Builder AI from the inspector. A field is edited as not mapped, a copy (a path
  picker over the sources), a fixed value, or an expression as JSON checked as it is typed.
- Open question: Create bill's vendor by name. QuickBooks and BILL take a vendor by id; a Reshape
  step can't look one up (it reads only its input), so a read step finding the vendor still comes
  first, and the proposal leaves `vendorId` for the operator or the Builder AI.
- Open question: whether a Reshape step's own output fields may nest (a record of records) beyond
  a list's items, and whether the operator may add fields the next step doesn't take (today the
  fields are the next step's, or the mapping's own with no next step).

#### Worker startup (2026-11-11)

Cloudflare refused the Worker (startup CPU over its limit, deploy of 3922f765): every tool's and
built-in skill's JSON Schema (`z.toJSONSchema`) and every pack manifest and template version
(`.parse`) was made while the modules loaded.

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| // DECISION: definitions built on first read | A tool spec's `input`/`output`, a built-in skill's schemas, a connector event's `payload`, a pack's manifest (`lazyParse`) and its template versions are computed on first read and kept, through enumerable memoised getters in place (`packages/core/src/lazy.ts`), so JSON, spreads, key order and equality are unchanged; senses' default registry is built on the first emit. A bad pack manifest now throws on first read, not at load: apps/api's tests build the platform with every pack. Zod schema construction, keepNames and pdf-lib's load stay as they are. |

`main`'s agent lab gallery, compact canvas, Fix with the Builder, Utilities, skills library tabs
and Sloan on by default were merged into this branch. Where both changed a screen, `main`'s
structure stands and this branch's behaviour is put back on it.

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|

Utilities' tabs are Feedback, Audit queue (wave 6, `/ops/utilities/run-audit`), Audit log and Requests. Website logins stay in the Library (`/ops/library/browser-sites`, titled Websites as on `main`); `main`'s `/ops/utilities/websites` and the old `/ops/browser-sites` and `/ops/run-audit` redirect. |
| // DECISION: the compact canvas on processes | A step card is `main`'s one row with its tooltip; a v4 kind has its own icon, the kind's words ("Save to records", "Change in QuickBooks Online") name it for screen readers and lead the tooltip, and a skill's kind (Deterministic or AI) stays on the row as a tag. Checks (a second check, notices) are marks like approval. The model a step runs on is in the tooltip. Triggers are one compact row each. Delete is in the side panel only. |

Wave 5's outcome wording runs first. A Reshape mapping's problem is kept as the validator writes it, since its editor shows it beside the mapping's field. |

A card's "how it runs" word is the skill's kind, Deterministic or AI, in place of Code, Task or Agent; the sheet still says how its mode runs. Each card keeps what it reads and browses, and the kind filter. |

An operator's deterministic skill (rule rows, no code) clones. The sheet offers Clone on AI task skills and an operator's deterministic skills only. |

### 1.87 BILL connector (owner: "bill.com integrated", 2026-11-10; no migration)

Connector `billcom` in `packages/connectors/src/billcom/` against a fake (`fakeBillcom` in
`@countersign/connectors/testing`); nothing has called BILL yet. What came from BILL's docs and
what is unchecked is in `billcom/NOTES.md`. Outside ARCHITECTURE v0.15's v1 scope, asked for by
the owner; ARCHITECTURE v0.16 should list it with the other connectors (§6.11).

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Connector | Id `billcom`, name "BILL", `auth: "api_key"` with three credential fields: `username`, `password` (secret), `organizationId`. So the portal's existing vault form ("Enter the login", `PUT /api/connections/billcom/credentials`, client admin only) takes it, with no new route or screen. Entities `Vendor`, `Bill`, `Payment`, `Document`. Registered everywhere, like Zoho, so it can be offered and built with. // DECISION |
| Whose login | The client admin makes a BILL user for us (the smallest role that does the job, not an administrator) and enters its login in the vault: encrypted with the client's own key, write-only, never in a response, log, step output, error or model call (invariant 13). The operator never sees it and has no route that takes it. The developer key is ours. // DECISION |
| Platform keys | `BILL_DEV_KEY` (secret, per environment) and `BILL_ENV` (`sandbox` or `production`, a var in `wrangler.jsonc`: sandbox locally and on staging, production in production) choose the host (`gateway.stage.bill.com` or `gateway.prod.bill.com`, `/connect/v3`). Without the key every tool refuses before anything is sent (`BillcomNotConfiguredError`, a refusal); the portal still offers the login form. A login BILL refuses for our key (its message names the dev key) is that refusal too, so a client's connection never goes to `error` over our key. // DECISION |
| Not available yet | Not shown for BILL without `BILL_DEV_KEY`: `canSignIn` in `apps/api/src/routes/portal.ts` lets every API-key connector with a form be set up whatever `isConfigured` says, and changing that would also change browser logins without `BROWSER`. Left as it is; the tools refuse with a plain reason. // DECISION |
| Sessions | Each tool call signs in when it first needs to (`POST /login` with the login read from the vault then, used once and kept nowhere), sends `devKey` and `sessionId` as headers, and signs out at the end (`POST /logout`, best effort). A skill run that holds sessions (`ConnectionContext.sessions`, v0.16) keeps one BILL session per connection for its calls and signs out when the run ends. A session BILL says has ended (401, or `BDC_1109`) is signed in again once and the request repeated (BILL refused it, so nothing was done); a second refusal, or a refused login, is `ReconnectRequiredError` (marked not written: BILL took nothing): the connection is marked as needing a person (`connection.needs_attention`), and entering the login again reconnects it. // DECISION |
| Errors | 400/422 → `BillcomInvalidInputError` (`kind: "invalid_input"`); 403 `forbidden`; 404 `not_found`; 409 `conflict`; 429 `rate_limited` (retryable). Every 4xx is not written (`notWritten: true`), so a step with `onError: continue` may go on. After a write is sent, no answer, a 5xx or an answer that doesn't read is `UnconfirmedWriteError` (the operator checks). On reads, 5xx and no answer are retryable. BILL's messages are cut to 300 characters with our key, the session and the password taken out. No throttle: about 20,000 requests an hour per key is reported, unchecked, and a 429 is retried by the step. // DECISION |
| Reads | `billcom.vendor.search` (start of name, email, archived only when asked), `billcom.vendor.get`, `billcom.bill.list` (vendor, payment status, due from/to, archived only when asked), `billcom.bill.get`, `billcom.payment.list` (vendor, bill, status), `billcom.payment.get`. Each output has `sources` (BILL's record ids); pages of up to 100 by BILL's `nextPage`. Our filters are applied again to the page BILL gives, so a filter syntax BILL reads differently never widens a result. Filter text has no quotes, backslashes or control characters; ids are letters and digits. A vendor's name, a bill's description and line text are data (invariant 9). // DECISION |
| Money | Amounts read through text into `numeric(14,4)` decimals, currency named (USD unless BILL names one); amounts written as JSON numbers from the decimal's text (`billcomJson`, as QuickBooks' `qboJson`). Bills we create must say `USD` until a non-US organization is checked. // DECISION |
| Writes | Each `external`, behind approval by default (invariant 8), run once per external action: `billcom.vendor.create`, `billcom.vendor.update`, `billcom.bill.create`, `billcom.bill.update`, `billcom.bill.archive`, `billcom.bill.attach_document`. No delete tool. One bill per action (BILL's `POST /bills/bulk` isn't used), so each is approved, checked and undone on its own. // DECISION |
| Once only | BILL takes no idempotency key that we know of. A retried write finds its own earlier one instead: a bill from the same vendor with the same invoice number (letters and digits), total and line count (when proposed, any bill with that vendor and number is a duplicate and refused); a vendor of the same name with every asked field, made in the last day (any other vendor of that name is refused: update it instead); a document of the same file name already on the bill; an update whose fields already have the asked values. Up to 1,000 of a vendor's open bills are read for this; more is refused. // DECISION |
| Bill create | Vendor, invoice number and date, due date, currency, lines (amount above zero, description, account), expected total: refused unless the lines add up to it. The approver rules read the amount (`expectedTotal`, `currency`). `before` names the vendor as BILL has it. A total BILL answers differently is unconfirmed (a person looks). // DECISION |
| Updates | Vendor: name, email, phone, account number, address. Bill: invoice number and date, due date, description; never amounts or lines. A bill with a payment scheduled or made (payment status other than `UNPAID`) is refused, as is an archived record. An `expectedUpdatedTime` that no longer matches, or a record changed since the approval (`proposedBefore.updatedTime`), is refused, not written. Both `invoice` fields are sent when either changes. // DECISION |
| Undo (R5) | `billcom.bill.create` is reversed by `billcom.bill.archive` (BILL's void: the bill stays, archived), guarded by the create's own `updatedTime`. Updates are `restore`: their own `undoInput` writes the before values back, guarded by the update's `updatedTime`; a field that was empty before has no undo (whether BILL clears a field on `null` is unchecked). Vendor create, archive and attach are `none`. // DECISION |
| Payments | `billcom.payment.create` (entity `payment`, verb `create`) is defined but refused: BILL pays only from an MFA-trusted session, and that needs the BILL user's second factor through our code service (`apps/mfa`), not built. It refuses when proposed and at the write, before BILL is called (`BillcomPaymentRefused`, a refusal, not written). The connector's starting matrix has `payment.create` off; a client can't turn it on (tighten only); the operator can, but the tool is `approval: "always"`, so no matrix, grant, step setting or mode lets it run without a person. Open: docs/open.md. // DECISION |
| Permission entities | `vendor` (read, create, update), `bill` (read, create, update), `payment` (read, create), `document` (create). Starting matrix: read auto, create and update approval, delete off, `entities.payment.create` off. // DECISION |
| Compliance | `billcom` is a processor (`PROCESSORS`, `CONNECTOR_PROCESSORS`, named "BILL"), unlike QuickBooks or Ramp: the calls go out under Mezonas' developer key and agreement with BILL, as Plaid's do. A client in HIPAA mode is refused its tools, and can't be offered it, until `billcom` is in `BAA_PROCESSORS`. Not added to the site's subprocessors page (the owner's call: docs/open.md). // DECISION |
| Web | No new screen. A mark (`B`, ink: BILL's logo isn't in Simple Icons), the money group on the portal's Accounts page, tool labels and the name "BILL" for run pages. The back office's Library → Connectors and the client's connections list it from the registry with its tools and default access. // DECISION |
| Tests | `packages/connectors/src/billcom/billcom.test.ts` (each read and write against the fake, sign-in and sign-in again on an ended session, the password in no output, log, error or request but the sign-in, approval by default, once-only retries, the created bill archived as its undo, unconfirmed writes, refusals not written, payments refused, HIPAA refusal, the starting matrix) and `apps/api/src/billcom.test.ts` (the vault login, the starting matrix, the back office's catalogue, a bill made once after the client's approval, nothing kept holding the password, the HIPAA policy). |
| Not built | Payments (MFA through `apps/mfa`); events or a poll for new bills; checking the login when it is entered; vendor archive, bill restore, vendor credits, BILL's own approvals, recurring bills. |

### 1.88 The vendor catalog: `vendor_item` (owner, 2026-11-11; the data and engine built, migration 0047)

The Purchasing area's next version. Today a vendor's version of a master item exists only as its
aliases (`item_alias`: vendor SKU and descriptions) and its prices (`price_observation`); pack
size, unit and anything not on an invoice have no home. The owner asked for a **vendor catalog**:
every item each vendor sells this client, specifically, with its last price.

| Topic | Plan |
|---|---|
| The table | `vendor_item`, one row per vendor per item the vendor sells (per client: `tenant_id`, forced RLS, invariant 1). Columns: `vendor_id`, `catalog_item_id` (the master item; **required**: a vendor item is created only once its master item is known, linked or new; an unresolved line stays with a person and has no vendor item yet), the vendor's `sku`, `name` (as the vendor writes it), `description`, `pack_size` and `vendor_uom` (e.g. bundle of 5), `std_per_vendor_uom` (decimal: how many standard units one vendor unit is, e.g. 5 sheets; the conversion rule for this vendor's item), `min_order_qty`, `lead_time_days`, `list_price` and `list_price_on` (when the vendor gave one), **`last_price`** (in the vendor's unit, as last invoiced or quoted), `last_price_std` (per standard unit), `last_price_on`, `last_price_source` (`invoice` \| `quote` \| `qbo_bill` \| `import` \| `person`, with the record id, invariant 10), `currency`, `preferred` (this vendor is the client's first choice for the master item), `status` (`active` \| `discontinued`), `ext`, timestamps. Unique per client on (`vendor_id`, `sku`) when a SKU exists. Money `numeric(14,4)` + currency (invariant 6). |
| How it relates | `catalog_item` (the master item, e.g. "3/4 in Baltic Birch Plywood 4x8") ← many `vendor_item` (Vendor A's "BB34-48", Vendor B's "PLY-18-BB") ← many `item_alias` (each wording or SKU a vendor has used, now pointing at its `vendor_item` as well as the master item). `price_observation` gains `vendor_item_id`, so every price row says which vendor product it was. Comparing vendors stays on the master item in standard units; a price is never compared across units without a conversion (invariant 7): the vendor item's `std_per_vendor_uom` is that conversion. |
| Last price | Updated by the same Save-to-records step that records a price (an `internal` tool, no approval by default): the newest observation by date wins; an older document never overwrites a newer price. The history stays in `price_observation`; `last_price` is the quick read. |
| How rows appear | Created when a line is matched (Look up existing, Match the unmatched, or a person) and no vendor item exists for that vendor and SKU or wording; filled further by quotes, QuickBooks bill lines and an import (a vendor's price list as CSV). Never by a skill directly: skills output data, a Save to records step writes (the skill model). |
| Tools | Reads: `materials.vendor_items.list` (one vendor's catalog: every item, last price, pack size), `materials.vendor_items.for_item` (every vendor's version of a master item, side by side in standard units, preferred first). Save to records: `materials.vendor_item.upsert`, `materials.vendor_item.set_preferred`, `materials.vendor_item.discontinue`. |
| Screens | Back office and portal Purchasing: a **Vendor catalog** per vendor (items, SKU, pack, last price and date, list price, preferred), and on a master item, its vendors side by side. Editable by the operator; the client sees it (it is their data) and can mark a preferred vendor if the operator allows (owner to confirm). |
| Migration | One, its own commit and PR, additive only: the new table, `item_alias.vendor_item_id` and `price_observation.vendor_item_id` (nullable), and a backfill of vendor items from existing aliases and the latest price per vendor and master item, so the catalog starts full. The previous Worker keeps working (new columns nullable, nothing removed). |
| Open for the owner | Whether the client may mark preferred vendors; whether a list price from a vendor's price list should alert when an invoice differs from it. |

**Master items are vendor-neutral** (owner, 2026-11-11): `catalog_item` holds only the generic
name, category, attributes and standard unit (e.g. "3/4 in Baltic Birch Plywood 4x8"), never a SKU,
a vendor's wording, a pack size or a price; those live on `vendor_item`. Every vendor item points at
exactly one master item; a master item has one or many vendor items. A master item with one vendor
looks almost like that vendor's item, minus the vendor specifics; a second vendor's version links to
the same master item, and vendors are compared there in standard units.

**The matching pipeline that goes with the vendor catalog** (owner, 2026-11-11). Built as skills and
steps under the skill model, as agents need them; templates are the owner's, built per agent.

| # | Step | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Match vendor: the invoice's vendor to our vendor record (vendor id, email domain, tax id, known names); none → a person, or Create vendor behind approval | Deterministic |
| 2 | Match by SKU at the vendor level: the line against this vendor's `vendor_item` rows by SKU, then by a description alias the vendor used before | Deterministic |
| 3 | Semantic match at the vendor level: semantic (vector similarity) search over this vendor's items, then the AI picks one or says "not in this vendor's catalog", with a confidence; then Check matches (the hard rules veto) | AI with retrieval, then deterministic |
| 4 | **Master item manager**: only for an item new to this vendor (steps 2–3 found no vendor item; a vendor item hit already gives its master item, so no other vendor is ever searched). Classifies it (category and attributes; the category parsers first, the model fills what they can't read), searches the client's **master items** (vendor-neutral; exact key attributes first, then semantic search) and decides: link to an existing master item, or create a new one | AI (deterministic parsing and lookup inside its reads) |
| 5 | Register item: a Save to records step writes the vendor item, its alias, and either the link or the new master item, and records the price (the vendor item's last price). **An optional approval** sits on this step, set per agent (off unless the operator turns it on), so a person can confirm new master items | Save to records |
| 6 | Anything unsure (low confidence, a hard-rule veto) → a person; their answer becomes an alias, caught at step 2 next time | If → person |

- DECISION (owner, 2026-11-11): the master item manager decides create-or-link itself; the approval
  that can confirm it is the optional approval on the Register item step, since a skill never writes.
- DECISION (owner left it to us, 2026-11-11): embeddings come from **OpenAI** (`text-embedding-3-large`
  at 1,024 dimensions, the existing `catalog_item.embedding` column's size; `text-embedding-3-small`
  if cost matters more), behind the existing `openai:` provider and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Why: OpenAI
  already holds a processor entry, its API offers a BAA with zero data retention for HIPAA clients,
  and its embeddings are well proven on short product text. Google's Gemini embeddings are the
  alternative if quality tests on the matching goldens favour them. Unchecked: current model names
  and prices (check OpenAI's pricing page). Embeddings are made when a master item or vendor item is
  saved; known lines never need one.
- DECISION (owner, 2026-11-11): the text embedded for a master item or a vendor item is one fixed
  template, **name + description + specs**, because a detail may appear in any of them:
  `Name: <name>` / `Description: <description as written; for a vendor item, the vendor's own
  wording>` / `Specs: category <c>; <attribute> <value>; …` (from the parsed attributes, units
  normalized, e.g. 3/4in (18mm)). Same order and labels for both, so comparisons are like for like;
  empty fields left out; prices, quantities, dates and order or shipping terms stripped; capped at a
  few hundred words; the embedding is made again when its name, description or specs change.

**Built: the data and the engine** (branch `vendor/data`, 2026-11-11; migration 0047). Platform
pieces only; templates are the owner's. Migration 0047 (its own commit): `vendor_item`,
`item_alias.vendor_item_id` and `price_observation.vendor_item_id` (nullable), forced RLS, no DELETE,
and the backfill. Embeddings on the `openai:` provider (`LlmTransport.embed`), declared in core
(`EMBEDDING_FEATURE`) and held to HIPAA by apps/api's model guard. Materials tools (`none` reads,
`internal` Save to records): `materials.vendor.match`, `materials.vendor_items.lookup`,
`materials.vendor_items.similar` and `materials.master_items.candidates` (each embeds the lines it
searches for), `materials.vendor_items.list`, `materials.vendor_items.for_item`;
`materials.vendor_items.register`, `materials.vendor_item.upsert`, `.set_preferred`,
`.discontinue`, `materials.embeddings.write`. Skills: Match vendor (`materials.match-vendor`) and
Match by SKU (vendor) (`materials.match-sku-vendor`), Deterministic; Semantic match (vendor)
(`materials.semantic-match-vendor`) and Master item manager (`materials.master-item-manager`), AI;
Check matches reused after each AI skill. Pattern: `vendorCatalogSteps` / `vendorCatalogProcess`
(`packs/materials/src/vendor/patterns.ts`). Back office: reports `materials/vendor-catalog` (an
item: one vendor's catalog) and `materials/master-vendors` (an item: a master item's vendors side
by side), actions `vendor-item-preferred` and `vendor-item-discontinue` (operator, audited).

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Pack size | // DECISION: `pack_size` is the vendor's words ("bundle of 5"); `std_per_vendor_uom` is the number that converts, so nothing parses words to compare prices (invariant 7). |
| A vendor item without a SKU | // DECISION: it is (vendor, master item, vendor unit), unique (hand-written index `vendor_item_no_sku_key`): a box and an each of one master item from one vendor are two vendor items. One preferred vendor item per master item (`vendor_item_preferred_key`); marking another clears the first. |
| No approximate vector index | // DECISION: searches are exact cosine distance over one vendor's items (or one client's master items in a category), narrowed by the btree indexes. An HNSW index orders every client's rows and filters after, so it can return fewer than asked (pgvector before 0.8 has no iterative scans; the local one is 0.6). An index is for when a client's catalog passes tens of thousands of items. |
| Backfill | // DECISION: one vendor item per SKU a vendor used (on its latest alias's item, a person's first), and one without a SKU per vendor and master item its wordings or prices name that no SKU covers; named as the vendor last wrote it. Priced in the master item's standard unit (`vendor_uom` the standard unit, `std_per_vendor_uom` 1), since every kept price is per standard unit. A wording or price is linked only where the vendor has exactly one vendor item for that master item (several SKUs: left null, never guessed); aliases and prices on a merged item are left. The last price is the newest by date. |
| The previous Worker | // DECISION: what it writes after 0047 has no vendor item; the new Worker resolves such an alias or price by its vendor and master item (the vendor's only item for it), and Register item links the alias when it next sees the wording. |
| Embeddings | // DECISION: `LlmTransport.embed` is optional; OpenAI's transport answers it from `/v1/embeddings`, routing sends it by model id, record/replay keeps it in the same fixture store under its own hash (`kind: "embedding"`), the client prices it by input tokens and reports it to `onEmbed` (kept apart from `onCall`, whose exchange is a message's), and an unpriced embedding model is refused before it is called. No transport: no vectors, and the searches fall back to names (trigrams); the model and the hard rules still decide. A test run makes none. |
| What is embedded | // DECISION: superseded by "The embedding text" below (name + description + specs, the owner's template). Still so: only items Register item made, or saved (never a known line's); idempotent by `ext.embedding.text`; backfilled items get theirs from `materials.embeddings.write` with `missing` (up to 500 a call). |
| Match vendor | // DECISION: the vendor id given, the document's purchase, the tax id (`vendor.ext.taxId`, letters and digits compared), the sender's email domain (`vendor.ext.domains`, one vendor only), the normalized name or a known name; a near name (trigrams) only when the agent's `min_name_similarity` is below 1 (default 1) and one vendor is that close. None: the pattern asks a person and stops. |
| Match by SKU (vendor) | // DECISION: the vendor's item with the line's SKU (a discontinued one too: the vendor invoiced it), then a SKU alias, then a wording alias of this vendor; an alias with no vendor item still gives its master item, and Register item makes the vendor item. |
| The semantic read | // DECISION: `materials.vendor_items.similar` scores this vendor's closest items (top 5 by embedding, then by name; one per master item) with the category's key attributes and lets the rules settle what they can (`decideByRules`): one equal item is a match; none that could be it, every required attribute stated, is new to this vendor; the rest are open for the model. The same document makes the same request (candidates in a fixed order), so recorded answers replay. |
| Check matches reused | // DECISION: Semantic match (vendor) answers in Check matches' shape, `new_item` meaning "not in this vendor's catalog", plus the `vendorItemId` it chose (a hint Register item checks: same vendor, same master item, never another SKU's item). The Master item manager answers in the same shape: `matched` links, `new_item` creates. The hard rules and the per-agent threshold are Check matches' own, unchanged. |
| Master item manager's read | // DECISION: `materials.master_items.candidates` takes the lines Check matches found new to the vendor: equal key attributes, close names, then close embeddings, in the line's category; one equal item links by the rules, none that could be it (every required attribute stated) creates by the rules, the rest go to the model. |
| Register item | // DECISION: one transaction for the document. A line decided before is left as it is (a retried step adds nothing). The vendor item is the SKU's, else the semantic hint, else the vendor's item for that master item in the line's unit, else its only one; else a new one named as the vendor wrote it, with the conversion when a rule exists. A SKU that names another master item: an agent's line goes to a person; a person's answer moves the vendor item. Each line gets an `item_match` row (the agent version, or the person), aliases with the vendor item, a price observation with the vendor item (per standard unit only with a conversion, invariant 7) and the vendor item's last price in its own unit (`invoice`, or `person`), the newer date winning (on the same date, the later). Unsure lines get an unsure row and go to a person. |
| A test run's Register item | // DECISION: it writes nothing: the work runs in its transaction and is rolled back, and the step answers what it would have written (the ids are the rolled-back rows'). |
| The person's answer | // DECISION: the person step (`ask`) shows the unsure lines with their candidates; its answer is `{ lines: [{ lineNo, catalogItemId }] }` or `{ lineNo, newItem: true }`, and "Save to records: your answer" registers it with the step's `by` as the person (`human` aliases, `decided_by_user_id`), so the next invoice's wording is caught at step 2. An answer without who gave it is refused. |
| Aliases | // DECISION: `learnAlias` takes the vendor item: an alias that keeps its master item keeps (or gains) its vendor item; one that changes master item takes the new vendor item (or none). |
| Recording prices elsewhere | // DECISION: `materials.prices.record` also sets the price's vendor item and its last price where the vendor catalog has one; it never makes a vendor item (Register item does). |
| The pattern's branches | // DECISION: an If repeats the steps after it in each branch with their own ids (`o-`/`s-`, then `m-`/`r-`): a step inside an If path isn't readable after it, and an AI skill with nothing to decide would still call its model. |
| New steps | // DECISION: `PackManifest.superseded` names a pack's skills another of its skills replaces for new steps (Look up existing → Match by SKU (vendor), Match the unmatched → Semantic match (vendor)); core's `newStepSkillReason` keeps them off the palette and the Builder, and stored steps keep running them. Built-in definitions (and their hashes) are unchanged. |
| Who sees the catalog | // DECISION: superseded by "The portal sees it" under The screens below. Was: the vendor catalog's reports are the back office's: the portal reads only the Materials reports its screens name (`portalReports`), until the owner decides what the client sees. Preferred and discontinued are operator actions (`/api/ops/clients/:id/packs/materials/actions/…`, audited, a refusal 422). |
| Tests | // DECISION: `apps/api/src/vendor-catalog.test.ts` runs the pattern through the workflow engine on hand-written replays (`fixtures/llm`, `handWritten`; the embeddings are character-trigram vectors): a known SKU, a known wording, a semantic hit, a line new to the vendor linked by the rules and one by the Master item manager, a new master item, a hard-rule veto that goes to a person, and the next invoice caught at step 2 with no model call and an older price not overwriting a newer one. The split's matching golden (`fixtures/matching`) covers the rules both paths share (`decideByRules`, `checkMatches`). |
| Start commit | The task named `4d66da642ab1…`, which doesn't exist; the branch starts at `4d66da64` (`4d66da649b54…`, `claude/busy-euler-cgu5kr`), the commit with that prefix and §1.88. |

Open, for the owner or a later stream:
- Whether the client may mark a preferred vendor (the actions are the operator's today), and
  whether a vendor's list price should alert when an invoice differs from it.
- The person step's card: the inbox shows an `ask` item's payload; a card that offers the master
  items to pick (and "a new item") and sends `{ lines: [...] }` is the screens stream's.
- When to embed what the backfill made: `materials.embeddings.write` with `missing` is a step; no
  cron runs it yet.
- Nothing writes `vendor.ext.taxId` yet (Match vendor reads it), and an invoice's tax id isn't read.
- An approximate vector index once a client's catalog is large (pgvector 0.8's iterative scans on
  Neon), and whether `text-embedding-3-small` is good enough on the goldens.
- A line in category `other` (no key attributes) never makes a new master item by the rules; the
  model or a person decides.

**Finished and verified** (branch `vendor/engine2`, 2026-11-11; no migration). The owner's word
that day: "build the platform … do the vendor catalog … forget about the skills, we will have to
refactor them after". So the skills stay as built (the two AI skills are built-in, not Library
skills; no new per-agent parameters beyond Match vendor's `min_name_similarity` and Check matches'
threshold); the rest of §1.88 is finished:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| The embedding text | // DECISION: one template for master items, vendor items and open lines (`packs/materials/src/vendor/embedding-text.ts`): `Name: …` / `Description: …` / `Specs: category <c>; <attribute> <value>; …`, empty lines left out. A master item: its name and its category and attributes (it has no description). A vendor item: the vendor's name and description as written, and its master item's specs (it is exactly that item, so its specs never depend on how one vendor abbreviates). An open line: its wording as the vendor wrote it as the name, no description, and the specs its category parser reads (Check matches' reading for a line new to its vendor). |
| What the specs say | // DECISION: the category, then the category's key attributes in its own order, then the rest by name; values lower case, underscores as spaces, `none` left out; the measured thickness beside the nominal one (`thickness 3/4in (19mm)`); a pack size left out (it is the vendor's packaging, `vendor_item.pack_size`). |
| What is stripped | // DECISION: from the name and the description: prices with a money mark, a currency or `@`, two-decimal prices per unit (`12.40/EA`), labelled prices; dates (ISO, matching separators, month names); labelled quantities (`QTY 40`, `shipped 12`, `B/O 3`); pack counts (`BOX OF 50`, `100/BOX`); order and shipping terms (PO and invoice numbers, FOB, net 30, ship via, freight, delivery, prepaid, collect, will call, drop ship, due on receipt, `terms:`). A bare fraction, a size, a thickness or a thread (`1/4-20`) is never touched. A description that only repeats the name is left out. |
| The cap | // DECISION: 300 words ("a few hundred"), labels counted; the description is cut first, then the name; the specs are kept whole. |
| Made again when it changes | // DECISION: what an item was embedded from is kept in `ext.embedding` with the template's name (`name-description-specs/1`). Due: no embedding, another template (or none named: everything embedded before this template), or, by ids, a different text. A vendor item's changed name, description or master item clears `ext.embedding` in the same update (`updateVendorItem`), so `missing` finds it; its old vector serves the searches until then. Register item hands the embeddings step the vendor items it moved to another master item as well as those it made. |
| Embedded when saved | // DECISION: `materials.vendor_item.upsert` embeds the item after its transaction (`usesModel`), and only when its text changed (a price or lead time embeds nothing). No model, or a test run: it stays due for `missing`. |
| Quotes fill the catalog | // DECISION: a quoted, available line whose request line has a master item sets the vendor's item for it (in the quoted unit, else its only one) to the quoted price (`quote`, the quote line as the record, the newer date winning) and its lead time. A quote never makes a vendor item, and a quote is still not a price observation. |
| QuickBooks bills fill the catalog | // DECISION: a bill line priced by the backfill names its vendor item on the price observation (the vendor's item in the standard unit, else its only one) and sets its last price (`qbo_bill`, the raw record), never making one. |
| A price in the vendor's unit | // DECISION: `priceForVendorItem`: the stated price when its unit is the vendor item's; else the standard-unit price when the vendor item is priced per standard unit (or names no unit), or through its `std_per_vendor_uom`; else the last price is left as it was (invariant 7). |
| The price list import | // DECISION: `materials.vendor_items.import` (Save to records): a vendor's price list as CSV text (columns found by header spellings, `PRICE_LIST_COLUMNS`) or rows, up to 5,000. Each row is the vendor's item by SKU, else by a SKU or wording alias of the vendor's, else by the master item the row names; it takes the list's name, description, pack, unit, units per pack, minimum, lead time and list price (dated `listPriceOn`). A row no master item is known for is listed `unplaced` and gets no vendor item; a SKU twice is skipped. It sets list prices, never the last price (a list isn't what was paid or quoted). It returns the vendor items it made or re-worded for the embeddings step. A test run rolls back. |
| The back office screen | // DECISION: Vendor catalog (`apps/web/src/packs/materials/VendorCatalog.tsx`), linked from the client's Packs tab, not named in the manifest (whose screens the portal reads): the vendors, one vendor's items (SKU, name, master item, pack, unit, last price with date and source, list price), a master item's vendors side by side per its standard unit, and Make preferred and Discontinue. English, as the back office's other screens. |

Still open, beside the list above:
- (Built below, "The screens".) The portal: §1.88's table says the client sees the vendor catalog (it is their data); today it is
  the back office's. A portal screen needs its words in the six languages; the owner to confirm.
- The skills: Semantic match (vendor) and Master item manager as editable Library skills, and the
  deterministic skills' values (vendor identifiers, shortlist size) as per-agent parameters, wait
  for the owner's skill refactor.
- An import screen (upload a price list in the back office) and a person's place for its unplaced
  rows; today the tool is a step an operator puts in a process.

**The screens** (branch `vendor/web3`, from `vendor/engine3`, 2026-11-11; no migration). Purchasing
gets its vendor catalog in the back office and, read only, in the portal; a master item's page;
the builder's palette and the skill editor for the vendor-first skills. Code:
`apps/web/src/packs/materials/VendorCatalog.tsx`, `apps/web/src/ops/skills/skill-form.ts`.

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| The portal sees it | // DECISION: the client reads its vendor catalog, read only (it is their data; the brief for this stream). The Materials manifest names the Vendor catalog as a screen (`/reports/materials/vendor-catalog`), so `screenReports` lets the portal read it, and apps/api adds `master-vendors` to the pack's `portalReports` for the catalog's item page. Preferred and discontinue stay operator actions (a client admin gets 403); the portal screens show no buttons. The responses carry no cost, prompt or instruction field (checked in `vendor-catalog.test.ts`). This replaces "Who sees the catalog" above. |
| One screen, two shells | // DECISION: `VendorCatalogView` and `MasterItemView` take an optional `clientId`, as the other Materials reports do: with one they read the back office's routes and show the operator's actions; without, the portal's. Every word but the two buttons is a message key (`materials.vendors.*`, `materials.item.*`) in the six languages; the back office reads them in English. |
| One vendor's items | // DECISION: SKU, their name, the master item (a link to its page), pack, the vendor's unit with what it holds in the standard unit ("bundle (5 × sheet)", from `std_per_vendor_uom`), last price, its date and source, list price (its date on hover), and a status word: Preferred, Discontinued or Active. The vendor is in the path (`…/vendor-catalog/:id`; none: the first), so a vendor's catalog can be linked; the picker counts every item its table lists. |
| Search | // DECISION: one box over the shown vendor's items: SKU, their name, the master item's name and the pack, case-folded in the reader's locale, on the page (a vendor's catalog is at most 2,000 rows, `vendorCatalog`'s cap). |
| A master item's page | // DECISION: `…/reports/materials/catalog/:id` in both shells (the Catalog's item names link there): its name, category, unit and attributes (the measured millimetres left out), and its vendors side by side per the standard unit, the preferred one first, then the active ones in the API's order (cheapest per standard unit, no conversion last), discontinued last (`preferredFirst`). A vendor's name opens its catalog. The back office has Make preferred and Discontinue on each row. |
| Tables | // DECISION: the analytical table (`dt dt-ana`), not the ledger: the ledger's column heads stick 24px down for a group row these tables don't have and covered their first row. The Catalog's table changes with them. |
| Palette | // DECISION: nothing new in the builder's logic: the catalog's `kind` labels the skills (Match vendor, Match by SKU (vendor), Check matches: Deterministic; Semantic match (vendor), Master item manager: AI), `palette: false` keeps Look up existing and Match the unmatched off, and Register item is a write on an `internal` tool, so it reads "Save to records" with approval off until the operator adds it (core `defaultWriteApproval`). The web gives the vendor catalog's tools plain names (`runs/labels.ts`: `materials.vendor_items.register` is "Register item"), and a pack's step tools sit under the pack's name in words ("Materials", `connectorLabel`) rather than its id. |
| AI skills in the editor | // DECISION: under the owner's word of 2026-11-11 ("forget about the skills, we will have to refactor them after") the two AI skills are still built-ins, so they open in the skill editor as any built-in AI skill does: the Library's Clone makes a shared operator skill draft and opens its page, with instructions, model, tests and versions. The editor now carries a skill's declared `reads` (the form's `reads`): shown ticked beside its tools, listed as tools it may use, kept as `reads` on save (unticked ones leave; a tool known to write never stays). Before, a clone's retrieval read was invisible and could not be removed. The API test clones both and saves a second version of each. |

the AI skills are editable Library skills, the deterministic ones built-in code with what may change
as per-agent parameters, only what the feature needs, no template made or edited, nothing already

and verified"), which nothing earlier in the repo recorded. Code: `packs/materials/src/vendor/skills.ts`,
`apps/api/src/routes/packs.ts` (`installLibrarySkills`), core `PackManifest.librarySkills`.

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| The AI skills are the Library's | // DECISION: Semantic match (vendor) (`custom:semantic-match-vendor`) and the Master item manager (`custom:master-item-manager`) ship as shared Library skills: operator skills (`custom:<slug>`, tenant_id null) the pack names in its manifest (`librarySkills`, core checks each is an operator skill) and apps/api installs once, v1 by the pack and published, the first time the pack is switched on for a client (as its templates are) and by "Update templates". From then on each is the operator's: Edit in the Library (instructions, model, parameters, tests, versions, publish); the pack never re-installs over it. The same instructions, model, schemas and reads as before, backed by the pack's tools (`materials.vendor_items.list`, `materials.catalog.search`). An agent references them as it does any shared skill: publishing a client agent snapshots the live version into the client (`shared:<slug>`), and a newer version reaches the client at the agent's next publish (invariant 11). The pattern (`vendorCatalogSteps`) names them. |

They never reached staging. |

| Match vendor's parameters | // DECISION: `match_on` (text, comma-separated words: document, tax id, email domain, name; default all four) is what Match vendor may match on; the order tried stays the code's (a purchase or a tax id is surer than a name), a vendor id given is always taken, and a word it doesn't know fails the step in plain words. A list has no parameter type of its own (number, text, date, amount, buckets), so it is text. `min_name_similarity` stays. |
| The shortlist sizes | // DECISION: `vendor_shortlist_size` and `master_shortlist_size` (1 to 10, default 5) are Match by SKU (vendor)'s parameters, the step that opens the vendor-level path: its output carries them (`shortlist`), and the pattern's two reads take them as their `limit` (`materials.vendor_items.similar`, `materials.master_items.candidates`). A read step gets no agent parameters of its own, and the AI skills come after their shortlist. `decideByRules` keeps as many candidates as the shortlist (`keep`). |
| The shortlist is filtered by code | // DECISION: what the AI skills choose from leaves out the candidates a key attribute rules out (`openLines(…, { withoutVetoed: true })`); the line keeps them for the person's card and for Check matches. Match the unmatched keeps its requests as they were (its stored steps replay). A line with every candidate ruled out goes to the model with none: it can only say new or unsure, and Check matches still holds a new item to every required attribute. |
| The last price in the vendor's unit | // DECISION: Register item and `materials.prices.record` reach the vendor item's last price through `priceForVendorItem` (the line's unit, else per standard unit through its conversion), and leave it as it was when they can't: a SKU's item priced per board foot never takes an MBF line's figure. This completes "A price in the vendor's unit" above. |
| A merge moves the vendor items | // DECISION: `mergeItems` moves the merged items' vendor items to the item that stays (`moveVendorItemsOnMerge`): a moved one loses `preferred` when that item already has a preferred one and forgets what it was embedded from; one without a SKU that would collide with the staying item's for the same vendor and unit is folded into it (its aliases and prices name the staying one, which takes its last price when newer) and discontinued where it was (`ext.foldedInto`; no DELETE grant). Register item also moves, without asking anyone, a vendor item left on an item merged into the line's. |
| Vendor-neutral master items | // DECISION: a master item Register item makes keeps no pack size (`withoutPackaging`), no `ext.firstDescription`, and, where its name falls back on the line's words (category `other`), none of the SKU, pack count, prices or terms (`neutralName`). The line's pack goes on the vendor item (`pack_size`, "100 per box"). A line converts by its own words over the master item's specs, never the master item's pack size, else by the vendor item's own conversion for that unit (`convertLine`), in Register item and in `materials.prices.record`; quotes and the purchase comparison still read the master item's attributes as before (an open question below). |

Rejecting stops the run, as before. Creating a vendor is not in the pattern: the person names one we have. This replaces "None: the pattern asks a person and stops" in "Match vendor" above. |
| The lead time's date | // DECISION: a quote's lead time is kept with its date (`ext.leadTimeOn`, no new column): an older quote never replaces a newer lead time; on the same date the later wins (`recordLeadTime`). |
| The embedding backlog | // DECISION: the pattern's embedding step also makes up to 50 of the client's due embeddings (`missing` beside the ids, `EMBED_BACKLOG_PER_RUN`): what the backfill made, or what was embedded under older text. No cron: the cost lands on the run, as every model call's does, and HIPAA mode holds through the run's model guard. An operator may still add a step with `missing` alone. |
| Labelled prices in the embedding text | // DECISION: a labelled price is a whole figure (never a fraction's numerator: "TOTAL 5/8 EDGE" stays), and EXT is a price label only with a colon, an equals sign or a money mark ("CDX PLYWOOD EXT 3/4" stays). The labelled forms are stripped first, with their label. |
| 0047's backfill run again | // DECISION: its first INSERT is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (the second already looked first), so a repair or a replay by hand adds nothing. 0047 has not reached staging or main, so it was changed in place, in a migration-only commit of its own (a fixup into its first commit would have flattened the branch's merges). |
| Not done: a line embedded twice | // DECISION: a line new to its vendor is embedded by the semantic read and again by the master items' read (their texts differ when Check matches added attributes). Carrying the vectors between the steps would put about 8 KB per line into every run's stored step outputs, for an embedding that costs a few millionths of a dollar; left as it is. |
